# Resource-bound inventory

Every cost input named by a public function's `@time` annotation, with how it is bounded. The inventory is reviewed, not derived: the checker proves only that it is complete against the annotations. Analysis and measured worst cases attach to these entries as they are produced; [timing and evidence](timing-and-evidence.md) defines how a claim becomes substantiated.

| Input | Bound | Limit | Enforcement | Masked | Profiles | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **waiters**: threads waiting on one wait queue | at most the live threads: a thread waits on at most one queue | base: 254 thread IDs; tiny: CONFIG_EMB_PRIORITY_COUNT - 1 threads | structural | yes | base: PRIORITY_FIFO insert walks from the tail, O(waiters), FIFO O(1); tiny: bitmap set O(1), first waiter O(1) or the raised-thread scan | SPEC-004 §11; the reference model's queue-order invariant |
| **timeouts**: armed timeouts | at most one per thread, so at most the live threads | as for waiters | structural | yes | base: doubly linked list, insert O(armed) from the tail, removal O(1); tiny: singly linked list, insert and removal O(armed) | SPEC-003 §5.1, SPEC-012 §13; the model's one-timeout-per-thread invariant |
| **owned**: mutexes one thread owns | not limited by the kernel: at most the mutex objects the application creates | application | application | yes | the same singly linked owned list on every profile; acquisition appends, release and recomputation walk it | SPEC-005 §2.3; A25 |
| **pi_depth**: inheritance chain hops (PI work) | CONFIG_EMB_PI_MAX_DEPTH hops; each hop recomputes O(owned) and requeues O(waiters) | CONFIG_EMB_PI_MAX_DEPTH (default 8, 1 to 32) | configuration | yes | checked builds fault at the limit, release builds stop propagating (no complete inheritance beyond it); deadlock detection inspects the same number of links | SPEC-005 §2.2, A25; m2-02-contract-review.md; model PI_MAX_DEPTH |
| **table_scan**: tiny raised-priority scan | CONFIG_EMB_PRIORITY_COUNT - 1 slots, only while some thread runs above its base priority | CONFIG_EMB_PRIORITY_COUNT, at most the architecture word width | configuration | yes | tiny only; base selects through the per-priority bitmap | ADR-036; kernel/sched/sched.c embk_sched_table_best |
| **reschedule**: a scheduling decision | O(1) on base (bitmap and per-priority lists); the table scan on tiny | see table_scan | structural | yes | one decision per preemption point; batch wakes reschedule once | SPEC-002 §6; KRN-WAIT-013 |
| **batch_wake**: waiters woken at once (destroy with EMB_OBJ_ABORT_WAITERS) | the waiters of the destroyed object | as for waiters | structural | yes | one section, one reschedule at the end | SPEC-004 §6.7; KRN-OBJ-001 |
| **thread_ids**: diagnostic identity scan at thread init | 254 IDs on list profiles, CONFIG_EMB_PRIORITY_COUNT - 1 on tiny | fixed per profile; EMB_ENOMEM beyond it | admission | yes | bitmap scan from the lowest ID | ADR-043; m2-02-thread-identity.md |
| **live_threads**: threads on the all-threads list | at most 254 (the ID space) | CONFIG_EMB_THREAD_LIST; the ID admission | admission | yes | base only (no list on tiny); walked by thread init and emb_thread_foreach | SPEC-008 §12; ADR-045 |
| **active_objects**: active objects of one type (semaphores, mutexes, event flags, condition variables, message queues, work queues, timers) | not limited by the kernel: the objects the application initializes | application | application | yes | with CONFIG_EMB_OBJ_LIST only (not on tiny); walked by init | ADR-045; m2-02-object-lifecycle.md |
| **item_copy**: bytes copied for one message queue operation | at most two items (a receive that refills from a waiting sender), each item_size bytes | CONFIG_EMB_MSGQ_MAX_ITEM (default 64, tiny 16); init refuses a larger item_size | configuration | yes | a byte loop under the object lock on every profile | SPEC-007 §2.2, KRN-IPC-011; tests/conformance/test_msgq.c |
| **armed_timers**: armed software timers | not limited by the kernel: the timers the application starts | application | application | yes | list scheduler only; insertion walks from the tail of the timer list (ADR-047), removal O(1); an expiry pass handles each due timer once | SPEC-003 §7, ADR-047; tests/conformance/test_timer.c |
| **stack**: bytes of one thread's stack | the stack size the application supplied | application | application | no | the high-water scan exists only with CONFIG_EMB_STACK_STATS; init fills the stack in checked and statistics builds | SPEC-008 §10; KRN-MEM-009 |
| **init_table**: entries of the initialization table | the EMB_*_DEFINE objects linked into the image | application, fixed at link time | application | no | prekernel only | KRN-OBJ-009 |
| **callbacks**: application callbacks the kernel calls (fault hook, trace sink, foreach visitor) | not bounded by the kernel | application | application | yes | the fault hook and the trace sink can run with interrupts masked; the foreach visitor runs under the scheduler lock | API-017; SPEC-015 |
| **port_action**: the port's fault action (halt or reset) | does not return | port | structural | yes | CONFIG_EMB_FAULT_ACTION | 03 §10; SPEC-011 §14 |
